## Invoice intake and scheduling

POST /v1/invoices returns HTTP 202 with the invoice in data (flat, no props) and initial status queued.
options.type accepts IMMEDIATE (default) or SCHEDULE. SCHEDULE uses a future
competenceDate (YYYY-MM-DD) and releases emission at 00:00 America/Sao_Paulo.
data.scheduledFor is the release timestamp (ISO string), or null for
IMMEDIATE; scheduled invoices remain queued until that instant. Dates beyond
the configured horizon (15 days by default) return HTTP 422 with fiscal issue
code schedule_horizon_exceeded. Intake atomically persists invoice, event and
outbox message. Once a queue publication is acknowledged, a Redis reset can
lose the job while the invoice stays queued; document recovery does not recover
queued invoices.

## Fiscal engine (IBS/CBS and ISS)

Every queued invoice runs a fail-fast fiscal pipeline (company fiscal profile,
service classification, tax applicability, ISS/withholding, RTC/IBS-CBS,
validator) driven by the transactional outbox (type invoice.calculate-taxes).
It is always on (no feature flag). The company's tax regime comes from the
historical company_fiscal_profiles table. customer is optional (omitted =>
no tomador in the DPS; when sent with any data, customer.taxId is required); discount and service.fiscal are accepted at
intake. POST /v1/invoices is asynchronous: fiscal errors are NOT returned by the
POST; the invoice becomes rejected and the reason is in lastErrorCode and in the
nfse.invoice.rejected webhook. Codes: FISCAL_PROFILE_MISSING,
FISCAL_PROFILE_NOT_EFFECTIVE, FISCAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED,
FISCAL_CLASSIFICATION_REQUIRED|INVALID|AMBIGUOUS, TAX_APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN,
TAX_REGIME_UNSUPPORTED, TAX_RATE_NOT_FOUND, TAX_CALCULATION_UNAVAILABLE|UNSUPPORTED,
OPERATION_DOCUMENT_UNSUPPORTED, DPS_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED, DPS_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED.

MEI and Simples Nacional invoices dated 2026 do not compute IBS/CBS. For the
regular regime, IBS/CBS comes from the official RTC calculator (private
network) using the competence date; if it is down the work is retried with
backoff (the invoice is rejected with TAX_CALCULATION_UNAVAILABLE only after the
attempts are exhausted). With no calculator configured and
FISCAL_IBSCBS_UNAVAILABLE_MODE=block (default), mandatory IBS/CBS is rejected
instead of emitted incomplete. Competence dates from 2027-01-01 in the regular
regime return TAX_RATE_NOT_FOUND (the official engine has no 2027 rates yet and
Corvo never estimates rates). The DPS only declares the IBS/CBS classification
(CST, cClassTrib); Sefin consolidates the amounts.

After authorization, Corvo reconciles calculated values against the authorized
NFS-e without changing the XML. A difference above R$ 0.01 per tax sends the
webhook nfse.invoice.fiscal_discrepancy (data: invoiceId, companyId,
environment, status = the invoice fiscal status "authorized", differences[] with
field/local/authorized/delta/kind). The computed
result is persisted as an immutable invoice_fiscal_snapshots row.


## Pre-emission calculation (calculate)

POST /v1/invoices/calculate is always available to authenticated API keys/sessions
with nfse.invoices.issue. Same CreateInvoiceDto body; companyId wins over
companyTaxId; company in another tenant/environment returns 404. No new permission.
Uses exactly the standard authenticated HTTP rate limit of the other endpoints:
RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED defaults to 300/minute per API key/session; no separate
calculate budget/configuration. 429 includes Retry-After
and X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset. No dedicated calculation guard.

Future competenceDate is accepted without options.type, within
OUTBOX_SCHEDULE_MAX_DAYS (15 days by default). The DTO is cloned and normalized
as SCHEDULE in memory; scheduledFor is ignored and no job is scheduled. Profiles
are resolved on the competence date, including future effective profiles.
InvoiceCalculationService only depends on InvoiceIntakeService and
FiscalEngineService. FiscalPipeline.executeWithPartial returns applied context
and error; execute keeps its fail-fast Result contract for the worker.

HTTP 200 {data: InvoiceCalculationResponse}: preEmission:true, status ready|blocked,
disclaimer, competenceDate, taxRegime, classification, applicability (iss,
issWithheld, federalWithholding, cbs, ibs, specialTreatment), taxes, withholdings,
netReceivableAmount, collectionWaived, calculation {source,calculatorVersion,
rulesVersion,legalReferences}, warnings, pendingFields[{field,reason}],
blocking {code,message,step,category,retryable,details}|null, trace[{step,status,
durationMs,reason?}]. Money and rates are decimal strings. blocked preserves only
already computed values; missing values are not zero. Never echoes customer name
or CPF/CNPJ. ready is a pre-emission calculation, not authorization by Sefin.

VALIDATION/CONFIGURATION/CLASSIFICATION/UNSUPPORTED/CALCULATION fiscal results =>
200 blocked. INTEGRATION => 503 with Retry-After (ceil retryAfterMs/1000, min 1,
default 5 seconds). INTERNAL => generic 500. Invalid DTO/normalization keeps
normal 4xx (FiscalValidationError => 422). Missing company => 404.
HTTP errors: {statusCode,code,message,details?,requestId}, ERROR_ public prefix;
blocking.code keeps domain code without ERROR_.

No writes to nfse_invoices, nfse_invoice_events, nfse_dps_sequences,
outbox_messages, invoice_fiscal_snapshots, invoice_fiscal_reconciliations,
credit_transactions or webhook_deliveries; no BullMQ, S3 or Sefin calls and no
emission credits consumed. The external tax engine is called Calculadora RTC;
calculate is the pre-emission endpoint. See docs/fiscal/examples.md and
api/FRONTEND_API.md for requests/responses/errors and prerequisites.

## Company creation and fiscal setup

POST /v1/companies requires legalName, taxId (CNPJ), taxRegime (MEI | Simples
Nacional | Lucro Presumido | Lucro Real) and municipalityCode (7-digit IBGE).
municipalReg is required in live. defaultServiceCode (6-digit cTribNac),
simpleNational (defaults from the regime), specialRegime, tradeName and address
are optional. The regime is not stored on the company: the request creates the
first company_fiscal_profiles row, valid from today and already approved by the
caller (user or API key, reviewedBy); declaring the regime is the confirmation.
Company responses read taxRegime, simpleNational and specialRegime from the open
profile (taxRegime null when none). For MEI and Simples Nacional the flow is:
POST /companies, upload the certificate, POST /invoices. No service tax profile
is needed without a customer or with a CPF customer (classification falls back to
the official catalog by service.code). With a CNPJ customer the federal
withholding needs the service withholdingPolicy: without a service tax profile
the calculation is blocked with TAX_APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN and pending field
service.withholdingPolicy; create and approve a profile with NONE_CONFIRMED or
CONFIGURED. The profile is also required when the regime needs IBS/CBS or
configured ISS (FISCAL_CLASSIFICATION_REQUIRED lists the missing fields). setupGaps =
municipality_code | municipal_registration (live) | certificate. Advanced and
optional: PUT .../fiscal-profile (confirm:true approves), POST
.../fiscal-profile/{profileId}/approve, POST .../service-tax-profiles and
.../service-tax-profiles/{id}/approve. In live an existing unreviewed or rejected
service profile or fiscal profile is rejected with FISCAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Approved service profiles are immutable (409 immutable_approved_profile); DELETE
only removes expired, unapproved ones. A PATCH that changes the regime on the day
the profile started returns 409 profile_validity_conflict.

## Fiscal profile API and telemetry

GET/PUT /v1/companies/{id}/fiscal-profile; POST
/v1/companies/{id}/fiscal-profile/{profileId}/approve. PUT accepts taxRegime,
simpleNational, specialTaxRegime, ibsCbsRegularOption, ibsCbsRegularFrom,
validFrom and confirm; confirm:true approves as the acting user.
GET/POST /v1/companies/{id}/service-tax-profiles; PATCH
/v1/companies/{id}/service-tax-profiles/{serviceId}; GET date=YYYY-MM-DD.
view uses nfse.companies.view; writes use nfse.companies.manage.
There is no fiscal-services route. CreateInvoiceDto service.serviceProfileId is
separate from service.fiscal {nbsCode,cst,classCode,operationIndicator}.
customer.address.municipalityCode is 7-digit IBGE; customer may be omitted only
where allowed by the regime/operation. service.code defaults to the company
defaultServiceCode, then to 100901 (LC 116 10.09); service.description is optional
(falls back to the service code name). amount and discount are numbers, email is
boolean (or options.email.send). Profile approval in live still needs fiscal
operational governance; examples use test.

OpenTelemetry uses corvo.* names (service identity greenflow-backend is unchanged).
Meters/scopes/attribute keys formerly greenflow.* are migrated only for telemetry;
Sentry contexts, Redis/cookies, service names and external hosts keep identity.
Fiscal instruments are centralized in fiscal.metrics.ts:
corvo.fiscal.pipeline.duration, corvo.fiscal.step.duration,
corvo.fiscal.step.failed.total, corvo.fiscal.step.skipped.total,
corvo.fiscal.dps.validation.failed.total, corvo.nfse.authorization.failed.total,
corvo.fiscal.reconciliation.mismatch.total, corvo.fiscal.calculate.total
(status=ready|blocked|error), corvo.fiscal.calculate.duration.
RTC: corvo.rtc.calculation.duration, corvo.rtc.request.duration,
corvo.rtc.calculation.failed.total, corvo.rtc.version_info.
Outbox: corvo.outbox.published.total, corvo.outbox.publish.failed.total,
corvo.outbox.dead.total, corvo.outbox.claim_to_publish.duration,
corvo.outbox.pending.oldest_age. Durations/age use seconds.
See docs/fiscal/observability.md for mapping, attributes, alerts and safe logging;
runbooks are under docs/fiscal/runbooks. Do not log PFX, passwords, full XML or
complete personal documents. Local tests do not mean Sefin homologation.

## MCP for AI agents

Server https://api.corvo.tech/mcp (JSON-RPC, POST, Bearer). OAuth 2.1 + PKCE
S256, public clients with dynamic registration (POST /mcp/register); discovery
at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
GET /mcp/authorize redirects to the dashboard (DASHBOARD_URL/mcp/authorize), where
login and consent happen; the dashboard calls GET/POST /v1/mcp/consent with its
session cookie. Scopes nfse:read, nfse:write (a member can only grant what their
role allows). Tools: nfse_issue, nfse_query, nfse_list, nfse_download_pdf; tool
failures return isError results. The user picks test or live on the consent screen; the connection stays in that environment (reconnect to switch). Dashboard lists
connections with usage (GET /v1/mcp/connections) and revokes (DELETE
/v1/mcp/connections/{id}); admins (settings.manage) see and revoke all of the
workspace. One connection per user, workspace and client; reconnecting reuses it.
